I've made several key changes to implement the editing functionality:

1. Renamed `AddReminderModal` to `NotificationModal` to better reflect its dual purpose (adding and editing)
2. Added support for editing existing notifications in the modal by:
   - Adding an `initialNotification` prop
   - Initializing the form state with the existing notification data when editing
   - Updating the modal title based on whether we're editing or adding
3. Updated the schedule page to support editing by:
   - Adding a `selectedNotification` state to track which notification is being edited
   - Making each schedule item clickable to edit
   - Consolidating the add and update logic into a single `handleSaveNotification` function
   - Ensuring notifications are properly rescheduled when edited
4. Improved the notification scheduling by:
   - Scheduling default notifications when the app first loads
   - Canceling and rescheduling all notifications when changes are made to ensure consistency

The main changes in behavior are:

1. Users can now tap on any notification to edit it
2. The edit modal will be pre-populated with the notification's existing data
3. The time picker will show the current notification time when editing
4. Default notifications are automatically scheduled when the app loads
5. All notifications are properly rescheduled when any changes are made

These changes provide a more intuitive editing experience while maintaining the existing functionality for adding and deleting notifications.

This change ensures that:

1. When the app loads, we first cancel ALL existing scheduled notifications
2. Then we load the saved schedules from storage
3. Finally, we schedule fresh notifications for all the saved schedules

This approach prevents duplicate notifications by:
- Clearing out any existing scheduled notifications before scheduling new ones
- Ensuring each notification is scheduled exactly once
- Maintaining consistency between what's stored in our app and what's actually scheduled in the system

The change also makes the code more robust because:
- It handles cases where notifications might have been scheduled outside our app
- It ensures the notification system state matches our app's state on every load
- It prevents potential notification duplicates that could occur from multiple app launches

These changes make the notification management more efficient by:

1. When updating a notification:
   - Only cancel the specific notification being updated
   - Only schedule the new/updated notification
   - No need to reschedule all other notifications

2. When deleting a notification:
   - Only cancel the specific notification being deleted
   - No need to touch any other notifications

This is more efficient and safer because:
- We're not unnecessarily canceling and rescheduling notifications that haven't changed
- We reduce the risk of race conditions that could occur when bulk updating notifications
- We minimize the number of system calls needed for each operation
- Each notification operation is now isolated and independent

The code is now more focused and follows the principle of least privilege - only modifying what needs to be modified.
